articles.title: Cuban Man in Miami Faces Charges for Filming Walmart Employee in Bathroom
articles.description: A 28-year-old Cuban national was taken into custody on Monday in southwest Miami-Dade, accused of taking photos and recording video of a Walmart employee inside a bathroom stall, as reported by the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office. The suspect, identified as Oscar Chamizo Martin, was caught around 12:15 p.m. at the store located at 14325 SW 268th St., in the Homestead area. He allegedly extended an orange-cased iPhone over the stall occupied by the victim. The Walmart employee noticed the device and, upon exiting the bathroom, confronted Chamizo Martin, who was the only individual present in that section at the time. Security cameras inside the Walmart recorded the employee leaving the restroom visibly distressed while calling for his manager. After the incident, Chamizo Martin left the store, but a sheriff's deputy contacted his employer and convinced him to return. Back at Walmart, the suspect denied taking any images, claiming someone else was responsible. However, he was found with an orange-cased iPhone that matched the victim's description exactly. Confronted with this evidence, he was arrested and taken to the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center (TGK), one of the main jail facilities in the county. As of Tuesday, Chamizo Martin remained detained with a $2,500 bond for the charge of digital voyeurism and also faced an immigration hold that could lead to deportation proceedings. In Florida, digital voyeurism is classified under statute 810.145, which prohibits the use of imaging devices to secretly record individuals in spaces where they have a reasonable expectation of privacy, like bathrooms or dressing rooms. For individuals over 19, the offense is considered a third-degree felony, punishable by up to five years in prison. This is not the first time Cuban nationals in Miami have faced serious criminal charges related to such behavior, amidst intensified cooperation between county authorities and federal immigration agencies. Florida has seen a series of voyeurism arrests in Walmart stores throughout 2025 and 2026 across various counties, including a recent case in Ocala just two days prior, where another man was apprehended for allegedly secretly recording minors in a similar setting. The immigration hold on Chamizo Martin indicates that immigration authorities have been notified of his arrest, which may result in additional consequences beyond the ongoing criminal proceedings.

articles.title: Former Orange County church employee sentenced to 40 years for secretly recording children using spyware
articles.description: Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A California man who previously worked for an Orange County church was sentenced to 40 years in prison for using spyware to secretly record children and directing juvenile victims to produce child sexual abuse material. Jacob Melvin Hart, 46, of San Juan Capistrano, had pleaded guilty to attempted production of visual depictions involving sexual exploitation of a minor and transportation of visual depictions involving the sexual exploitation of minors, the U.S. Attorney's Office said. An investigation revealed that Hart had previously worked as an IT consultant for Crossline Community Church in Laguna Hills, where he had access to children, prosecutors said. He also managed the church's audiovisual and computer technology operations. Hart provided laptops equipped with spyware to several children at the church, allowing him to remotely activate the computers' cameras without the children's knowledge. Using the spyware, he secretly recorded at least eight children and possessed sexually explicit depictions of those children, prosecutors said. In June 2025, while returning from a mission trip to Haiti, Hart was arrested at Miami International Airport by U.S. Customs and Border Protection. An inspection of his electronic devices revealed an extensive collection of child sexual abuse material, including images and videos that he had directed children in Russia to create. On July 29, 2026, Hart was sentenced to 40 years in prison. Federal prosecutors said that in 2006, Hart was convicted in Oregon of invasion of privacy after secretly installing a hidden camera in a girls' locker room at a Christian children's camp. In January 2026, two alleged victims filed separate lawsuits against Crossline, accusing the church of negligence, after they were allegedly recorded by the refurbished computers given to them by Hart, the Orange County Register reported. One of the female victims said that in 2013, she needed a new computer at the start of a school year. Hart reportedly offered to give her a refurbished model, which the family accepted. Investigators said Hart had installed software enabling the girl's computer to be remotely accessed and monitored, according to the suit. The computer captured images of the girl nude in the bathtub and getting in and out of the shower. Another female victim said Hart gave her a computer in 2023 so she could assist with editing videos for the church. The computer later recorded the girl showering and getting dressed, her lawsuit said. The suits claimed that multiple children accepted a laptop computer from Hart, with the church's knowledge. Lawyers also alleged that church officials were aware of Hart's previous conviction in Oregon when they hired him in 2012, claiming he had disclosed his conviction and a pornography addiction to his new bosses, the O.C. Register reported. Several church staff members have since resigned following the lawsuits. Church representatives said they are cooperating with law enforcement on the investigation. In a statement to the Register, church officials said, "The Elders of Crossline Community church are deeply grieved by the actions of Jacob Hart and the pain and suffering he has caused, especially to the victims. We have provided regular updates to the church, launched an independent investigation and strengthened our internal safety protocols, volunteer screenings and hiring processes." "This defendant weaponized technology and abused positions of trust to invade children's most private spaces and sexually exploit them," said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones. "The 40-year sentence imposed on Jacob Melvin Hart means he will likely spend the rest of his life in federal prison. It protects children from a calculated predator and demonstrates that we will pursue those who produce and solicit child sexual abuse material, whether their victims are here at home or across the world." pendingReview.title: Delivery driver accused of filming man in Walmart restroom near Homestead, police say
pendingReview.description: Peter D'Oench is a reporter for CBS4 News. He came to CBS4 from WKRN in Nashville. A 28-year-old man was arrested and charged with video voyeurism at a Walmart near Homestead, an incident that has left customers alarmed. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office responded to the store, located at 14325 S.W. 268th St., on Monday morning after a victim reported being filmed while using the restroom. The victim told authorities he noticed someone reaching over a stall to retrieve an iPhone with an orange cover. He confronted the suspect, who was the only other person in the men's restroom at the time. According to an arrest affidavit, store security footage captured the suspect, Oscar Chamizo-Martin, entering the restroom with the victim. The victim exited the restroom "visibly upset" and alerted a manager. Authorities reported that Chamizo-Martin, who identified himself as a delivery driver, left the store but was later contacted through his employer. He was arrested after returning to the location. While Chamizo-Martin denied recording, investigators noted he possessed a cell phone matching the description provided by the victim. In bond court, a judge set bond at $2,500 and issued a stay-away order prohibiting Chamizo-Martin from returning to the Walmart. Because of an active U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) hold, Chamizo-Martin will remain in custody. Once the local case is resolved, he will be transferred to federal authorities. Walmart customers expressed shock at the incident. "That is disrespectful when you are in the stall," said customer Nini Florin. "It is a public place. You think you would be safe. It is your own little abode using the restroom." "I don't know why people can't just use the bathroom in peace in public," added customer Alex Sanchez. In a statement, Walmart's press office said, "The safety and security of our associates and customers is a top priority. We will continue to cooperate with local law enforcement as they investigate." Video voyeurism is a third-degree felony in Florida. A conviction can carry a maximum penalty of five years in prison, five years of probation, and a $5,000 fine. Penalties may be increased if the suspect is a repeat offender or if children are victimized.

pendingReview.title: Convicted West Virginia sex offender pleads guilty to buying 50+ GB of child porn
pendingReview.description: (WOWK) -- A previously convicted West Virginia sex offender has pleaded guilty to a new child pornography charge. According to the U.S. Department of Justice, Justine L. Wiegand, 34, of Kenova, pleaded guilty on Monday to a charge of receipt of child pornography. The DOJ says he is accused of purchasing child sexual abuse material from a messaging app at least nine times between December 2023 and January 2025. Wiegand's sentencing has been set for Nov. 23, 2026. He faces at least 15 and up to 40 years in prison, followed by five years to life on supervised release, as well as a fine of up to $250,000. "Sexual exploitation of children is one of the worst and most damaging crimes in our country," said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department's Criminal Division. "Those who participate in these crimes damage lives, rob innocence, and create emotional wounds that last a lifetime. Whether you produce child sexual abuse material (CSAM), distribute it, or access it via subscriptions to messaging apps, we will find and prosecute you subject to mandatory minimum penalties, as in the case of this repeat offender." According to court documents and statements, Wiegand contacted a messaging app user in December 2023, and the user gave him options for purchasing videos and links to files of child sexual abuse material. The DOJ says as part of his guilty plea, Wiegand admitted to paying $25 for a package of 160 videos and four file folders on an online file hosting service that contained more than 50 gigabytes of child sexual abuse material. Court records state Wiegand requested similar content from that messaging app user and other users at least eight more times through January 2025. The DOJ says evidence showed that during one of those instances, Wiegand had allegedly asked a messaging app user if they had any rape videos. According to the DOJ, Wiegand also had video on his cell phone from a hidden camera that he had set up depicting an approximately-10-year-old girl undressing and showering in a bathroom. The DOJ says that video was saved to his phone "no later than" July 29, 2025. The DOJ says he also had several other videos and photos of child sexual abuse material on his phone. At the time of these crimes, Wiegand was serving home confinement for a May 5, 2023, conviction of third-degree sexual assault, according to the DOJ. Court records state that Wiegand admitted that the 14-year-old victim in that case was depicted in child sexual abuse material found on Wiegand's private cloud storage service.

pendingReview.title: Residents, police raise concerns about recurring drone sightings: 'We need someone to stop this'
pendingReview.description: WEST BRANDYWINE, Pa. (WPVI) -- Residents in a Chester County neighborhood say recurring drone activity over their homes has left them concerned about privacy and searching for answers. West Brandywine police say an investigation is still underway into the aircraft's nighttime flights. One resident, who requested to remain anonymous, said she has encountered the drone multiple times. "The first one came in December. I was hoping it was random, and then I started seeing them more and more often. We found out some other neighbors also had seen them flying over their bedroom and bathroom windows, specifically like the skylights," the woman said. Neighbors say they have spent months wondering who is operating the aircraft. The resident said the drone frequently appears near her home late at night: "Between 10 and 11 p.m., they're always over my bedroom and bathroom window, just hovering." West Brandywine police said the aircraft have repeatedly appeared over homes and skylights in the Wallace area of the township, including as recently as Monday. Police said officers have witnessed the activity themselves, notified the Federal Aviation Administration and are treating the matter as a possible invasion-of-privacy investigation. The resident described the activity as intrusive. "So many people defend the rights of drone flyers, which is crazy. If there was someone with a 20-foot ladder up to your windows looking in, would you be defending them? It's a peeping Tom; that's 100 percent what it is." An aviation expert not involved in the case said flying a drone over a neighborhood is not automatically illegal and noted that federal regulators, not local authorities, control most airspace regulations. Bradford Ryll said potential surveillance activity could raise legal concerns. "It is possible that if there is some kind of surveillance activity happening, that might be a violation of Pennsylvania law," Ryll said. Police said the drone's operator has not contacted the department. That could be because they are not required to. However, Ryll said if investigators can prove images are being captured inside private homes, the situation could become actionable if the pilot is identified. In a statement, police said in part, "The use of a drone to invade someone's personal privacy will not be tolerated, and the maximum allowable penalties will be pursued." Concern remains among some residents as the investigation continues. "With four kids, the concern is there and very real as to why this person is hovering over our neighborhood," said Shannon Kaschak, who, like her neighbors, has many unanswered questions. The anonymous resident said she has installed cameras, an alarm system, drapes and blinds, and covered skylights to help protect her privacy. "We need someone to stop this; it's gotta stop." Police continue to ask residents to report any sightings. Action News also contacted the FAA and is awaiting a response.
